payload.summary: The catalogue publication cannot run as tooled: no candidate can ever be canonical while every registry row is owner-scoped and nothing has been published, so the reconciliation planner refuses for a reason that is not the one it reports
payload.detail: WHAT HAPPENS. scripts/build-site-content-reconciliation-plan.ts, run against a fresh operator export (843 records, activeReleaseId e4a1dd29, initialized=false, expected=actual=843), reports: owner rows 222, logical groups 222, published groups 843, groups not published 3, TRIAGE SNAPSHOTS 0, needs owner review 222, adoptable 0, identical duplicates 0. It then refuses, telling the operator that 222 groups diverge from the published snapshot and that choosing between them is a clinical judgement. WHY THAT MESSAGE IS MISLEADING. Nothing diverged. buildRegistryReconciliationReport can only mark a group adoptable when canonicalCandidate returns a candidate, and canonicalCandidate delegates to reconcileCanonicalPublicSiteContent, which requires ALL FOUR of publicationState='published', renderedByPublicSite=true, explicitlyReconciled=true and rowOwnerId=null. Measured on live: clinical_registry_records has 222 service rows and 54 form rows, ALL with a non-null owner_id; site_content_publications has 0 rows; site_content_public_records has 0 rows. So no candidate can satisfy those conditions in this state, no triage snapshot is ever built, and every group falls through to divergent_requires_administrator_review by construction. The count 222-of-222 is an artefact of the state, not a measurement of drift. WHY IT MATTERS. The handover (docs/site-content-publication-handover.md) tells the owner the order is export, then reconciliation plan, then the administrator records it. Step 2 cannot produce output, so the owner would follow the documented order and hit a refusal that blames the corpus. Worse, the refusal is the kind that invites someone to 'fix' it by relaxing the triage, which would mark owner-scoped rows canonical for a clinical publication - exactly the judgement the script exists to refuse. WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEEDED, and it is a design decision rather than a bug fix. The reconciliation/adoption path is built for rows that are ALREADY public and whose identity is settled; it adopts them into the control plane. This corpus has never published anything through the control plane at all - the epoch-zero freeze lives only in site_content_release_records. So the question to settle before any more tooling is whether initial adoption is the right mechanism here, or whether these 222 owner-scoped service rows need a first-publication path that makes them public and unowned through the administrator flow. Do NOT resolve it by loosening reconcileCanonicalPublicSiteContent. SMALLER, SEPARATE: the planner should say what it actually found. A refusal that reports 'triage snapshots 0' alongside 'needs owner review 222' should state that the two together mean nothing was comparable, not that 222 things disagreed.
payload.source: live read 2026-09-21 of clinical_registry_records, site_content_publications and site_content_public_records, plus a run of scripts/build-site-content-reconciliation-plan.ts against the real export
